name: preempt-rt-mmci-hardirq

change.description: For the board-opt-in bounded PIO path, keep MMCI unthreaded under PREEMPT_RT and use a dedicated raw spin lock while leaving all other MMCI instances on normal RT semantics.

constant_contract.kernel: Linux 5.15.211-rt97 ARM NOMMU FDPIC XIP from QSPI
constant_contract.data: VFAT on the same SD card at approximately 1.95 MHz
constant_contract.latency: TIM3 CH1 PB4/D3 hardware reference to priority-99 SCHED_FIFO kthread PG7/D4 response

deployment.verification: U-Boot verified the staged CRC and the programmed QSPI image CRC during the subsequent clean boot.

boot.driver_mode: using hard IRQ and raw lock for bounded PIO writes

fat_repair.observation: fsck.fat printed its version and then made no progress or serial output for more than four minutes while checking the first read.

hammer.reason: The first fsck read stalled, so neither FAT durability nor a full workload could be validated.

decision: Do not use the hard-IRQ compatibility mode. The next storage experiment should use STM32 DMA2 streams 3/6, as the LXP/oveRTOS implementation does, and remove st,poll-write-fifo so MMCI retains normal PREEMPT_RT IRQ threading.
interpretation: Restoring hard-IRQ and raw-lock semantics removes the earlier write-error behavior but introduces a request-completion stall. It is therefore neither correct nor an acceptable latency tradeoff.
